                             O R D E R
 Heard learned Senior Counsel/Counsel for the parties.
2. At the outset, Mr. Jayant Mehta, learned Senior Counsel
representing  the  Respondent  No.99  (Manipal  Cigna  Health
Insurance) submits that Mr. Joydeep Saha, Managing Director and
Chief Executive Officer of the Insurance Company has been
8

## Page 19

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
called today as there was some miscommunication with regard to
him filing an affidavit. He submits that he is present and has
filed  his  personal  affidavit.  Thus,  personal  presence  of
Mr. Joydeep Saha is dispensed with, for the present. 
3. The matter started on an innocuous issue of whether a
vehicle which was said to be the cause of an accident, was the
real vehicle involved in the said accident. But as the events
unfolded, an exercise has been taken pan India, pursuant to the
order of this Court in the present proceedings to unearth
whether fraudulent claims are being filed, that too, in a fixed
pattern, where the same vehicle is shown to be involved in
multiple accidents, which results in such frivolous claims
being  allowed.  This  appeared  to  be  a  fraud  of  enormous
proportion and has persuaded the Court to enlarge the scope of
the present proceedings to unravel and also to check such
fraudulent claims, which ultimately result in not only undue
financial stress on the Insurance Companies, but also on the
system and one of the fallouts is that the common genuine
consumer  has  to  pay  a  higher  premium,  just  because  the
Insurance companies have to ensure their financial viability. 
4. At this juncture, we called upon Mr. Jagdish Chandra
Solanki, learned counsel to assist the Court on various issues
as he has experience in these matters, and has also had the
privilege of working in an Insurance Company, where, according
9

## Page 20

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
to  him,  he  came  across  various  irregularities,  acts  of
commission/omission  and  lack  of  oversight,  which  had
facilitated the frauds to perpetuate. He has suggested that the
Court may implead the Insurance Regulatory and Development
Authority (IRDA) under the Ministry of Finance, Government of
India, as a party respondent, as all the Insurance Companies
ultimately are governed by the regulations made by IRDA. He
further submitted that a common portal be developed where all
insurance claims be shown so that there can be ready access by
all the Insurance Companies with regard to any claim which may
be filed, so as to cross check the records of the other
companies as to whether such vehicle/person/institution/entity
is involved in repeated and multiple claims being made on a
regular basis. He submits that as of now two portals, i.e.,
VAHAN and SARATHI are available, which basically cater to data
collection and the submission is that if they can also be
integrated with the common portal, there can be ease of
tracking all such claims, both with regard to the veracity of
the accident, if any, the vehicle involved and the exact place
where the accident has occurred.  
5. A suggestion has also been made by Ms. Rupali Samuel,
learned Standing Counsel for the State of Tamil Nadu that the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
has a portal named E-detailed Accident Report (EDAR), which
10

## Page 21

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
tracks accidents on the National Highways across India. It was
submitted that if the same can be integrated with the other
portals which carry such data as also with the portal of the
IRDA,  the  authenticity  and  correctness  of  the  accident
occurring and the vehicle involved can be addressed more
readily and conveniently. 
6. Learned counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh submits that
a special SIT was constituted for the purposes of verification
of these claims relating to complaints being received by the
insurance companies indicating potential frauds, was pursuant
to the orders passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in
SLP(Civil) No.1110/2017 titled “Safiq  Ahmad  vs.  ICICI  Lombard
General  Insurance  Co.  Ltd.  &  Ors. ”. She submits that till
recently,  2188  complaints  were  received,  in  which,  upon
inquiry, over 1029 were investigated and 231 FIRs have been
lodged against 533 accused persons. We appreciate the action
taken by the State of Uttar Pradesh in the matter. We are
informed  that  other  States  might  have  also  followed  the
procedure. However, for the present, we are not going into that
individually. 
7. A fresh direction is issued to all the States to constitute
a special dedicated SIT for such purposes at the State level.
All complaints by the Insurance Companies be forwarded to the
said body, which will be looked into expeditiously. The States
11

## Page 22

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
are directed to provide sufficient hands to the SIT for
completion  of  the  investigations.  The  States  should  also
disclose with regard to the procedure they have adopted for
investigating in the present matter. 
8. At this point, the Court deems it appropriate to indicate
that it shall be the responsibility of the Insurance Companies
that all claims indicative of fraud are forwarded to the SIT
and pick and choose approach is not done. The Court will hold
the top most management of the concerned Insurance Companies
accountable if it is found that there has been selective
forwarding of the cases to the SIT of the concerned State. Any
recommendation by the SIT or FIR lodged against the officers of
the Insurance Companies shall also be taken cognizance of and
appropriate action on the departmental side shall also be
initiated against such officials by the concerned Insurance
Companies, without any delay. 
9. The Insurance Companies shall file their affidavits as to
what action has been taken by them in terms of what has been
indicated hereinabove, both with regard to the cases referred
to the SIT, as also the in-house action taken against the
officials, who may play a role prejudicial to the interest of
the Company and facilitated the fraud which was attempted or
committed by the parties concerned.
10. Let the IRDA be impleaded as respondent no.104. Similarly,
12

## Page 23

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
the Ministry of Finance, though the Secretary, Union of India
be impleaded as respondent no. 105; the Ministry of Road
Transport and Highways through the Secretary be impleaded as
respondent no.106; the General Insurance Council (GIC), which
we are informed is the overall body under the IRDA which is
responsible for coordinating among the Insurance Companies and
also  laying  down  general  policies,  be  also  impleaded  as
respondent no.107.
11. Notices shall be sent to the newly added respondents by the
Registry forthwith and they shall also file their affidavits
giving details of what is their responsibility at present, how
they discharge the same and what, according to them, could be
the steps which are required to be taken, meaning thereby that
they shall give their suggestions how to handle or take care of
the  situation,  which  the  Court  is  taking  note  of  and
considering in the present proceedings.  
12. The matters be listed on 23.09.2026 at 2.00 p.m.
13. On the next date, learned counsel for all the parties
should be ready with a one page note which would be a
precis/summary  of  their  affidavits  for  the  Court’s  ready
reference. 
14. After the order was dictated, a suggestion has come from
Mr. Solanki, learned counsel, that wherever the Insurance claim
is  negated  by  the  concerned  MACT  on  the  ground  of
13

## Page 24

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
fraud/collusion, the concerned Insurance Company would carry
out an in-house appraisal of the said case and also forward
details of the same to the SIT of the concerned State in which
the incident has occurred, for action. We find the suggestion
to be useful and relevant. Accordingly, a direction is issued
to the Insurance Companies that such matters where the claim is
negated on the ground of fraud or collusion, the said Insurance
Company shall immediately forward the details of the said case
to the SIT of the State where the claim is raised and also
carry out an in-house investigation with regard to whether
there was contributory collusion by its officers.
15. Details  of  the  same  shall  also  be  disclosed  in  the
affidavits to be filed by all concerned. 
16. At this juncture, we reiterate that in our order dated
18.03.2026 at paragraph no.7 we had indicated that all the
respondents may take note of the action taken by the State of
Odisha pursuant to the directions of this Court in the present
proceedings and accordingly, come up with their own modalities.

                             O R D E R
 Heard learned Senior Counsel/Counsel for the parties.
2. At the outset, Mr. Jayant Mehta, learned Senior Counsel
representing  the  Respondent  No.99  (Manipal  Cigna  Health
Insurance) submits that Mr. Joydeep Saha, Managing Director and
Chief Executive Officer of the Insurance Company has been
called today as there was some miscommunication with regard to
24

## Page 35

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
him filing an affidavit. He submits that he is present and has
filed his personal affidavit. Thus, personal presence of Mr.
Joydeep Saha is dispensed with, for the present. 
3. The matter started on an innocuous issue of whether a
vehicle which was said to be the cause of an accident, was the
real vehicle involved in the said accident. But as the events
unfolded, an exercise has been taken pan India, pursuant to the
order of this Court in the present proceedings to unearth
whether fraudulent claims are being filed, that too, in a fixed
pattern, where the same vehicle is shown to be involved in
multiple accidents, which results in such frivolous claims
being  allowed.  This  appeared  to  be  a  fraud  of  enormous
proportion and has persuaded the Court to enlarge the scope of
the present proceedings to unravel and also to check such
fraudulent claims, which ultimately result in not only undue
financial stress on the Insurance Companies, but also on the
system and one of the fallouts is that the common genuine
consumer  has  to  pay  a  higher  premium,  just  because  the
Insurance companies have to ensure their financial viability. 
4. At this juncture, we called upon Mr. Jagdish Chandra
Solanki, learned counsel to assist the Court on various issues
as he has experience in these matters, and has also had the
privilege of working in an Insurance Company, where, according
to  him,  he  came  across  various  irregularities,  acts  of
25

## Page 36

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
commission/omission  and  lack  of  oversight,  which  had
facilitated the frauds to perpetuate. He has suggested that the
Court may implead the Insurance Regulatory and Development
Authority (IRDA) under the Ministry of Finance, Government of
India, as a party respondent, as all the Insurance Companies
ultimately are governed by the regulations made by IRDA. He
further submitted that a common portal be developed where all
insurance claims be shown so that there can be ready access by
all the Insurance Companies with regard to any claim which may
be filed, so as to cross check the records of the other
companies as to whether such vehicle/person/institution/entity
is involved in repeated and multiple claims being made on a
regular basis. He submits that as of now two portals, i.e.,
VAHAN and SARATHI are available, which basically cater to data
collection and the submission is that if they can also be
integrated with the common portal, there can be ease of
tracking all such claims, both with regard to the veracity of
the accident, if any, the vehicle involved and the exact place
where the accident has occurred.  
5. A suggestion has also been made by Ms. Rupali Samuel,
learned Standing Counsel for the State of Tamil Nadu that the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
has a portal named E-detailed Accident Report (EDAR), which
tracks accidents on the National Highways across India. It was
26

## Page 37

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
submitted that if the same can be integrated with the other
portals which carry such data as also with the portal of the
IRDA,  the  authenticity  and  correctness  of  the  accident
occurring and the vehicle involved can be addressed more
readily and conveniently. 
6. Learned counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh submits that
a special SIT was constituted for the purposes of verification
of these claims relating to complaints being received by the
insurance companies indicating potential frauds, was pursuant
to the orders passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in
SLP(Civil) No.1110/2017 titled “Safiq  Ahmad  vs.  ICICI  Lombard
General  Insurance  Co.  Ltd.  &  Ors. ”. She submits that till
recently,  2188  complaints  were  received,  in  which,  upon
inquiry, over 1029 were investigated and 231 FIRs have been
lodged against 533 accused persons. We appreciate the action
taken by the State of Uttar Pradesh in the matter. We are
informed  that  other  States  might  have  also  followed  the
procedure. However, for the present, we are not going into that
individually. 
7. A fresh direction is issued to all the States to constitute
a special dedicated SIT for such purposes at the State level.
All complaints by the Insurance Companies be forwarded to the
said body, which will be looked into expeditiously. The States
are directed to provide sufficient hands to the SIT for
27

## Page 38

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
completion  of  the  investigations.  The  States  should  also
disclose with regard to the procedure they have adopted for
investigating in the present matter. 
8. At this point, the Court deems it appropriate to indicate
that it shall be the responsibility of the Insurance Companies
that all claims indicative of fraud are forwarded to the SIT
and pick and choose approach is not done. The Court will hold
the top most management of the concerned Insurance Companies
accountable if it is found that there has been selective
forwarding of the cases to the SIT of the concerned State. Any
recommendation by the SIT or FIR lodged against the officers of
the Insurance Companies shall also be taken cognizance of and
appropriate action on the departmental side shall also be
initiated against such officials by the concerned Insurance
Companies, without any delay. 
9. The Insurance Companies shall file their affidavits as to
what action has been taken by them in terms of what has been
indicated hereinabove, both with regard to the cases referred
to the SIT, as also the in-house action taken against the
officials, who may play a role prejudicial to the interest of
the Company and facilitated the fraud which was attempted or
committed by the parties concerned.
10. Let the IRDA be impleaded as respondent no.104. Similarly,
the Ministry of Finance, though the Secretary, Union of India
28

## Page 39

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
be impleaded as respondent no. 105; the Ministry of Road
Transport and Highways through the Secretary be impleaded as
respondent no.106; the General Insurance Council (GIC), which
we are informed is the overall body under the IRDA which is
responsible for coordinating among the Insurance Companies and
also  laying  down  general  policies,  be  also  impleaded  as
respondent no.107.
11. Notices shall be sent to the newly added respondents by the
Registry forthwith and they shall also file their affidavits
giving details of what is their responsibility at present, how
they discharge the same and what, according to them, could be
the steps which are required to be taken, meaning thereby that
they shall give their suggestions how to handle or take care of
the  situation,  which  the  Court  is  taking  note  of  and
considering in the present proceedings.  
12. The matters be listed on 23.09.2026 at 2.00 p.m.
13. On the next date, learned counsel for all the parties
should be ready with a one page note which would be a
precis/summary  of  their  affidavits  for  the  Court’s  ready
reference. 
14. After the order was dictated, a suggestion has come from
Mr. Solanki, learned counsel, that wherever the Insurance claim
is  negated  by  the  concerned  MACT  on  the  ground  of
fraud/collusion, the concerned Insurance Company would carry
29

## Page 40

SLP (C) NO.5582/2023
out an in-house appraisal of the said case and also forward
details of the same to the SIT of the concerned State in which
the incident has occurred, for action. We find the suggestion
to be useful and relevant. Accordingly, a direction is issued
to the Insurance Companies that such matters where the claim is
negated on the ground of fraud or collusion, the said Insurance
Company shall immediately forward the details of the said case
to the SIT of the State where the claim is raised and also
carry out an in-house investigation with regard to whether
there was contributory collusion by its officers.
15. Details  of  the  same  shall  also  be  disclosed  in  the
affidavits to be filed by all concerned. 
16. At this juncture, we reiterate that in our order dated
18.03.2026 at paragraph no.7 we had indicated that all the
respondents may take note of the action taken by the State of
Odisha pursuant to the directions of this Court in the present
proceedings and accordingly, come up with their own modalities.
17. The CMD of the following Insurance companies were required

issued vide order dated 06.04.2026:

Hon’ble  Mr.  Justice  Joymalya  Bagchi  pronounced  the
judgment of the Bench comprising Hon’ble the Chief Justice of
India, His Lordship and Hon’ble Mr. Justice Vipul M.Pancholi.
Delay condoned. Permission to file MAs is granted.
In terms of the signed reportable judgment, which is
placed on the file, 
(i) Writ Petitions and Miscellaneous Applications are 
disposed of. 
(ii) Civil Appeal Nos.381-382 of 2025, challenging
the  prospective  operation  of  Madras  High  Court
judgment in Fatima vs. Union of India, are dismissed.
(iii) The appeal filed by the State of Tamil Nadu
against the judgment in Fatima, being C.A. No.8253 of
2026, may be disposed of in light of the findings and
observations in this judgment. 

## Page 55

(iv)  Pending Interlocutory Application (s), if any,
shall stand disposed of.
13.           
SLP (C) No.8187 of 2025
1. The SLP assails the judgment dated 19.03.2025 passed by the
Bombay High Court in Writ Petition (L) No. 8110 of 2025, whereby
the closure of a mall was upheld. Since the challenge is not
confined to a prayer for post facto EC under the 2017 Notification,
but  also  raises  other  grounds,  the  matter  is  factually
distinguishable. Accordingly, the Registry is directed to de-tag
the matter and list it before appropriate Bench for hearing as per
Rules.

judgment of the Bench comprising Hon’ble the Chief Justice of
India, His Lordship and Hon’ble Mr. Justice Vipul M.Pancholi.
Delay condoned. Permission to file MAs is granted.
In terms of the signed reportable judgment, which is
placed on the file, 
(i) Writ Petitions and Miscellaneous Applications are 
disposed of. 
(ii) Civil Appeal Nos.381-382 of 2025, challenging
the  prospective  operation  of  Madras  High  Court
judgment in Fatima vs. Union of India, are dismissed.
(iii) The appeal filed by the State of Tamil Nadu
against the judgment in Fatima, being C.A. No.8253 of

## Page 68

2026, may be disposed of in light of the findings and
observations in this judgment. 
(iv)  Pending Interlocutory Application (s), if any,
shall stand disposed of.
13.
SLP (C) No.8187 of 2025
1. The SLP assails the judgment dated 19.03.2025 passed by the
Bombay High Court in Writ Petition (L) No. 8110 of 2025, whereby
the closure of a mall was upheld. Since the challenge is not
confined to a prayer for post facto EC under the 2017 Notification,
but  also  raises  other  grounds,  the  matter  is  factually
distinguishable. Accordingly, the Registry is directed to de-tag
the matter and list it before appropriate Bench for hearing as per
Rules.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
Madhya Pradesh
1. We have perused the affidavit dated 31 st August, 2026 filed by the State
of Madhya Pradesh.
2. A fresh dispute is being raised by the State through Mr. Sarthak Raizada,
learned counsel, that Teacher Eligibility Test 1 qualification is mandatory for
appointment as teachers in Primary Schools even for Children with Special
Needs relying on the notification dated 23rd August, 2010 of the National Council
for Teacher Education2.
3. It is, however, not in dispute that of the 257 (contractual) special
teachers/guest teachers, 116 have been found to possess both Rehabilitation
1 TaET
2 NCTE
14

## Page 83

Council of India3 as well as TET qualifications. 
4. We propose to consider the concern expressed by the State upon hearing
the RCI and the NCTE, the need wherefor has arisen because of a letter dated
14th August, 2023, issued by the Under Secretary to the Director (Elementary
Education), Directorate of Education, Rajasthan which has been tendered across
the bar.  The contents of the letter are as follows:
“I am directed to refer to your letter No. क्रमममांक :- शशिवविरम /पमरमां / वनियय. - 2 /
982 / निविवीनि  अ.भ. / विव. - 2 / 2022-23  dated 05.07.2023 on the subject
cited  above  and  to  say  that  the  minimum  qualifications  for
appointment of special teachers is laid down by Rehabilitation Council
of India (RCI), Qutab Institutional Area, New Delhi and not by the NCTE.
2. This issues with the approval of Competent Authority.”
5. In view of such letter of the NCTE, we require the presence of the RCI and
the NCTE on the next date.  
6. However, for the present, we direct the State to appoint the 116
candidates who have been found to possess both RCI and TET qualifications in
accordance with the order dated 07th March, 2025 as well as subsequent orders
passed by this Court from time to time. 
7. The concern expressed by the State shall be considered in the presence of
learned counsel for the RCI and NCTE on 29th September, 2026. 
8. The steps taken for compliance with this order with regard to appointment
shall be apprised to this Court on the next date.
Union Territory of Lakshadweep
9. None appears for the Union Territory (Administration) of Lakshadweep. 
10. Fresh notice be issued to the Administrator requiring representation of the
Union Territory before us on the next date. 
3 RCI

O R D E R 
1. Heard. 
2. Leave granted. 
3. Respondent no. 1 was posted as an English 
Teacher in the “XXX” School. Pursuant to a written 
complaint lodged by the appellant , the father of the 
victim on 23rd July, 2025, FIR No. 40 of 2025 came 
to be registered at the Women Police Station, Kaithal, 
for offences punishable under Section 8 of the 
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 
2012, Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the 
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, 
and Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. 
It was  alleged that respondent no. 1 had molested 
and sexually harassed the appellant’s minor 

## Page 135

2 
 
daughter, aged 14 years, who was studying in 10th 
Grade in the said school. 
4. During the course of investigation, it came to 
light that respondent no. 1, in order to destroy the 
evidence of his complicity in the crime, removed the 
DVR of the CCTV camera installed in  the school 
without permission.  A complaint to this effect was 
lodged by the Principal of the School before the In -
Charge of Police Post, Sangatpura, Kaithal on 23 rd 
July, 2025. 
5. Respondent no. 1, apprehending his arrest in 
connection with the aforesaid FIR, approached the 
Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Special Court, 
Kaithal, who rejected the said application by order 
dated 22nd August, 2025. 
6. Being aggrieved, respondent no. 1 approached 
the High Court by way of an application under 
Section 4 82 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha 
Sanhita, 2023  seeking anticipatory bail . By order 
dated 1 st September, 2025, the High Court granted 
interim anticipatory bail to respondent no. 1, 
directing him to join the investigation. 
7. While on interim anticipatory bail, respondent 
no. 1 is stated to have accessed and operated the 
computer of the school clerk without authorisation. 

## Page 136

3 
 
It is further alleged that he subsequently made 
telephonic communications to the victim. In this 
regard, complaints dated 3rd and 5th September, 2025 
were submitted before the Superintendent of Police, 
Kaithal.   
8. On 10 th September, 2025, upon joining the 
investigation, respondent no. 1 is stated to have 
made a disclosure statement, wherein he admitted to 
acts of sexual assault and threats against the victim. 
The status report dated 16 th October 2025, filed by 
the State before the High Court, further referred to 
CCTV footage recovered from a pen drive, which 
purportedly showed the victim coming out of the 
Language Lab, followed shortly thereafter by 
respondent no. 1 emerging from the same room.   
9. The High Court , however, by the impugned 
order dated 23 rd January, 2026 made the interim 
order of anticipatory bail absolute . The said order is 
subjected to challenge in th e present  appeal with 
special leave. 
10. During the course of submissions, learned 
counsel representing respondent no. 1 pointed out 
that pursuant to the grant of pre -arrest bail to him, 
respondent no. 1 has been released on regular bail by 

## Page 137

4 
 
the trial Court vide order dated 3rd April, 2026 upon 
accepting his bail bonds. 
11. We have heard and considered the submissions 
advanced by learned counsel for the parties and have 
gone through the material available on record. 
12. Having considered the nature and gravity of the 
allegations levelled against respondent no. 1 and 
more particularly, the fact that respondent no. 1, 
while working as a Teacher in a School, is alleged to 
have sexually assaulted a student  and thereafter 
attempted to tamper with evidence and intimidate the 
victim during the pendency of investigation , in our 
opinion, it was not a fit case warranting grant of pre-
arrest bail to respondent no. 1. The impugned order 
cannot, therefore, be sustained. 
13. We are of the opinion that respondent no. 1 has 
been released on regular bail only in compliance of 
order of pre -arrest bail granted to him by the High 
Court and hence, the said development is of no 
consequence.  Since the order of pre -arrest bail is 
itself being set aside, the automatic consequence 
thereof would be the cancellation of regular bail and 
the bail bonds furnished by respondent no. 1. 
14. Consequently, the impugned order is set aside. 
Respondent no. 1 shall surrender before the trial 

## Page 138

5 
 
Court within a period of two weeks from today and 
shall thereafter be at liberty to apply afresh for 
regular bail, which application shall be considered on 
its own merits  and in accordance with law  without 
being prejudiced by this order. 
15. The appeal is allowed accordingly. 
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand 
disposed of.

“2. We direct the Secretaries to the Government of
India, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of
Personnel,  Public  Grievances  and  Pensions,
Department of Personnel and Training to submit
individual affidavit(s) detailing the steps taken
thus far for implementation of the directions
issued by this Court vide the judgment and order
dated 23.05.2025 passed in Civil Appeal No.13104
of 2024 (Sanjay Prakash & Ors. versus Union of
India & Ors.)
3. In the compliance affidavit(s), it shall also
be mentioned as to how many officers have been
brought on deputation to the Central Armed Police
Forces (CAPFs), cadre wise, up to the level of
Senior Administrative Grade (SAG), after passing
of the judgment and order dated 23.05.2025.”

Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, it is
stated that 46 Indian Police Service (IPS) officers have
been brought on deputation to the Central Armed Police
Forces (CAPFs) upto the level of Senior Administrative
Grade (SAG) after passing of the judgment on 23.05.2025.
The  statement  furnished  by  the  said  respondent  is
extracted hereunder:
IPS OFFICERS BROUGHT ON DEPUTATION TO CAPFS UPTO THE LEVEL
OF SENIOR ADMINISTRATIVE GRADE(SAG) AFTER 23.05.2025
Force SP DIG IG TOTAL
BSF - 8 5 13

CRPF - 4 5 9
ITBP - 3 3 6
SSB 2 2 3 7
3. Before we pass necessary order(s), we direct the
Secretary to the Government of India, Ministry of Home
Affairs to explain the above statement, for bringing in
IPS  officers  on  deputation  to  the  five  CAPFs;  what
procedure was followed before bringing the above officers
on deputation i.e., whether any requisition was made by
the  borrowing  department  for  deputation  etc.  and  the

the judgment of this Court directing that the number of

upto the level of Senior Administrative Grade (SAG) should

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The  respondent(s)-claimant(s)  preferred  claim  petition(s)
seeking the benefits available to the dependents of the deceased,
who was the head of the family, under the Mukhyamantri Kisan and
Sarvahit Bima Yojana. Under the terms of the said Scheme, the claim
was required to be raised within a period of three months from the
date of occurrence of the incident.
2. However, in the matter of G autam Yadav Vs. State of Uttar
Pradesh & Ors.,  Writ Petition No. 15983 of 2020, decided on
11.11.2020, the Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad held the limitation prescribed under the Scheme for
preferring the claim to be unreasonable and directed that the said
period be extended by a period of three years.
3. The order passed by the High Court in Gautam Yadav(supra) was
assailed  before  this  Court  in  Special  Leave
Petition(Civil)No.7647/2021, which has been disposed of during
Samadhan Samaroh (Lok Adalat) leaving open the question of law.
4. In the meanwhile, all the respondent(s)-claimant(s) in the
present batch of Special Leave Petitions have preferred claim
Petition(s) before the concerned Authority. The permanent Lok
Adalat allowed the claim(s) and awarded different amounts in favour
of the respondent(s)-claimant(s). Aggrieved by the said awards, the
petitioner-Insurance Company preferred Writ Petition(s) before the
High Court, which came to be dismissed by the impugned order(s),
relying upon the judgment in Gautam Yadav(supra).
5. It is informed that, pursuant to the interim order(s) passed

## Page 178

4
by this Court, the claim amount(s) have already been paid to the
respondent(s)-claimant(s).
6. In view of the above, there is no purpose in keeping the
present Special Leave Petitions pending. The same are, accordingly,
disposed of without interfering with the impugned order(s), in the
facts and circumstances of the present cases.
7. In case, in any of the Special Leave Petitions, the whole or
any part of the claim amount remains unpaid, the petitioner-
Insurance Company shall comply with the order of the High Court
within a period of three months from today.
8. Pending application, if any, shall also stand disposed of.
(VARSHA MENDIRATTA)                        (AKSHAY KUMAR BHORIA)

O R D E R
Heard Ms. Manita Verma, learned counsel appearing for the
petitioners  and  Mr.  Vinay  Navare,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent.
2. At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioners points out
that in the order of this Court dated 01.09.2026, it was recorded
that the matter was listed today on the joint request of the
parties.

## Page 180

2
SLP(C)No.9076/2023
3. It is submitted that no such request for adjournment was made
by learned counsel for the petitioners.
4. Having regard to the aforesaid, the reference to a joint
request of the parties in the order dated 01.09.2026 stands
modified to read - ‘The matter be listed on 03.09.2026’.
5. The petitioners are aggrieved by the order impugned, inasmuch
as  it  has  nullified  the  entire  result  of  the  Disciplinary
proceedings against the respondent by not interfering in the Single
Judge’s Order dated 20.04.2018 holding that no loss was caused to
the Bank, whereas, on record, it was proved that loss has occured.
6. Learned  counsel  for  the  petitioners  submits  that  this
observation being made by the learned Single Judge and the Division
Bench in the impugned order upholding that portion of the order on
the one hand, and then giving liberty to the petitioners to pass a
fresh order after considering each of the contention of the
respondent against the second show cause notice, on the other hand,
is meaningless, for the reason that no authority can go beyond the
findings recorded by a Court, much less, a Writ Court. It was
contended that though the Appellate Authority had passed a reasoned
and detailed order, but still the petitioners shall once again
revisit the matter and pass a fresh order.
7. In  response,  Mr.  Vinay  Navare,  learned  Senior  Counsel
appearing for the respondent submits that the contention of learned
counsel for the petitioners is erroneous. It was submitted that no
loss has actually been caused to the Bank as can be seen from the

## Page 181

3
SLP(C)No.9076/2023
fact that even the charge-sheet did not mention the same. Moreover,
it was submitted that the consideration of the second show-cause
notice filed by the respondent was ex facie  not fair, as there is
neither  any  discussion  nor  any  reason  given  as  to  why  the
contentions  raised  by  the  respondent  were  rejected  by  the
Disciplinary Authority. However, learned Senior Counsel submitted
that if the Court is inclined to remand the matter, fixed time
frame should be indicated for the reason that the respondent has
already superannuated on 31.12.2020.
8. Having regard to the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition
stands disposed of with a direction to the Disciplinary Authority
to pass a fresh and reasoned order in terms of the directions given
in  the  order  impugned.  However,  we  make  it  clear  that  the
Disciplinary Authority shall not be handicapped/fettered by any of
the observations/directions/findings recorded, either in the order
of the learned Single Judge dated 20.04.2018 or in the impugned
order dated 30.01.2023 and shall take a fresh and independent view
of the matter. The same be done within three months from today,
after giving due opportunity of hearing, if so asked for by the
respondent,  in  accordance  with  law.  The  interim  order  dated
15.09.2023 to continue till the passing of the fresh order by the
Disciplinary Authority.
9. After  the  order  was  dictated,  learned  counsel  for  the
petitioners submitted that in terms of the previous directions of
the Court to bring on record the actual loss suffered by the Bank
due to the conduct of the respondent, the same has been brought on

## Page 182

4
SLP(C)No.9076/2023
record by way of an affidavit.  Be that as it may, as copy of the
same has already been handed over to learned counsel for the
respondent, it shall be open to the respondent to give his response
on the same also.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for
the appellant and the learned counsel appearing
for the respondent-State. 
3. The appellant seeks regular bail in connection
with  FIR  No.226/2024,  registered  at  Police
Station  -  Sadar  Jalandhar,  District  Police
Commissionerate, Jalandhar, Punjab and has been
charge-sheeted for the offences punishable under
Sections 15, 25, 27-A, 29 and 31 of the Narcotic
Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 and
Sections 25, 25(1)(b), 54 and 59 of the Arms
Act, 1959.
4. In pursuance of the earlier order passed by us
1 SLP(CRL.) No.9339/2026

## Page 196

on 17.07.2026, the material witnesses have been
examined by the Trial Court. The appellant has,
admittedly, been under incarceration for nearly
one year and seven months. Suffice it to state
that  the  continued  incarceration  of  the
appellant is not required, particularly, in the
light  of  the  examination  of  the  material
witnesses having been completed.
5. In such view of the matter, we are inclined to
set aside the impugned order passed by the High
Court and grant bail to the appellant.
6. Accordingly,  the  impugned  order  stands  set
aside,  and  the  appellant  is  granted  bail,
subject to the terms and conditions that may be
imposed by the concerned Trial Court.
7. I.A.No.232928/2026 stands disposed of and the
appeal stands allowed, accordingly.
8. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
(Civil Appeal Nos.        /2026)
(Arising out of SLP (C) No(s). 25005-25010/2025)
SANJAY SINGH                                       Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
GYANMANJARY RAO & ORS.                             Respondent(s)
O R D E R
                     
1. Heard.
2.  Leave granted.
3.  The parties are referred to as per the rank before the High Court in
the writ petition. The writ applicants/petitioners whose appointment came to be
set-aside was the subject matter of the writ petition which came to be allowed
by Order dated 16.05.2023 with liberty to redo the exercise. Hence, after
issuing show cause notices against the writ applicants their services were
terminated on 13.02.2024 on the ground of the selection process was tainted,
which was again challenged in Writ Application No. 5091/2024 before the
jurisdictional High Court who by Order dated 09.07.2024 stayed the direction
issued by the State on 04.07.2019 as well as the Termination Order dated
13.02.2024. For alleged non-compliance of this order contempt proceedings
were initiated and by the impugned order/judgment the contemnors were
directed to appear in the contempt proceedings, which is the subject matter of
the present appeals. Being aggrieved by the order of the learned Single Judge
1

## Page 204

the State filed writ appeal(s) in which stay was sought for and was not granted.
Hence, being aggrieved by the same and also being aggrieved by the order of a
Contempt Court directing them to appear in person for framing of the charge,
the present appellants have filed these appeals. This Court by Order dated
08.09.2025 has stayed further proceedings in Contempt Application (Civil) No.
640/2025 which is in operation till date. 
4.  Though several contentions have been urged and rebutted, the fact
remains that the writ application is still pending before the learned Single Judge.
Hence, continuation of the present proceedings would only be permitting the lis
to be pending at all levels.  Hence, in these circumstances, we deem it apt and
appropriate to continue the stay of contempt proceedings which was granted
on  08.09.2025, till the disposal of the Writ Application Nos. 5091/2024,
2760/2024 and 2758/2024 and request the High Court to dispose of the writ
applications expeditiously on merits. In view of the aforesaid order, the writ
appeal(s) as well as the contempt application(s), would not survive for
consideration and the jurisdictional Courts can consign the same to records.
5. In view of the above, these appeals stand disposed of.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of. 
...................J
(ARAVIND KUMAR)
                  ..................J.
                  (VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)
NEW DELHI;
August 21, 2026.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The core issue that arises for consideration in these matters  
pertains to the constitution and composition of the State Bar  
Councils and the Bar Council of India in accordance with the  
provisions  of  the  Advocates  Act,  1961  and  the  rules  framed  
thereunder.
2. Pursuant to various orders passed by this Court in M. Varadhan 
v.  Union  of  India  and  Anr. , W.P. (Civil) No. 1319 of 2023,  
elections to the State Bar Councils have since been conducted.  
Additionally  vide orders  dated  04.12.2025  and  08.12.2025  in  
Yogamaya  M.G.  v.  Union  of  India  and  Ors. , W.P. (Civil) No.  
581/2024, it was directed that there shall be 30% representation  

## Page 209

3
for the women members of the Bar in every State Bar Council. Out of  
this 30% representation, 20% was to be directly elected, whereas  
10% was to be co-opted.  
3. When the issue of the manner and modalities of co-option  
arose, this Court  vide order dated 04.08.2026 in  Yogamaya  MG  
(supra) resolved that the Chief Justices of the jurisdictional High  
Courts in consultation with the newly elected members of the  
respective State Bar Councils, shall nominate two women members,  
preferably from among former women judges of the respective High  
Courts or senior women members of the Bar.  
4. It goes without saying that once the co-option exercise is  
complete, the composition of the State Bar Councils shall stand  
notified. In order to rule out any uncertainty, we therefore deem  
it appropriate to request all the Chief Justices to complete the  
exercise of co-option within a period of two weeks. The composition  
of the newly-elected State Bar Councils shall be notified within  
one week thereafter.
5. Following this, each State Bar Council shall be required to  
elect its Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, office-bearers as well as  
“one member by each State Bar Council from amongst its members” as  
member of the Bar Council of India under Section 4(1)(c) of the  
Advocates Act, 1961. These elections, therefore, are also required  
to be conducted at the earliest. Consequently, we direct the newly-
constituted  State  Bar  Councils  to  elect  their  statutorily  
prescribed office-bearers, including their representative to the  
Bar Council of India, within a period of two weeks from the date of  
notification of their composition.

## Page 210

4
6. All the State Bar Councils are directed to file compliance  
reports in this regard.
7. On  receipt  of  these  compliance  reports,  the  issue  re:  
constitution of the Bar Council of India under Section 4 of the  
Advocates Act, 1961 shall be considered.
8. Meanwhile, Mr. Maninder Singh and Mr. S. Guru Krishna Kumar,  
learned Senior Counsel representing the Bar Council of India and  
its office-bearers, have fairly stated that the learned Attorney  
General for India and the learned Solicitor General of India shall  
be actively associated with the policy-making process leading to  
any policy decision that may be taken before the new Bar Council of  
India is constituted.
9. Issue notice to all the State Bar Councils.
10. Dasti, in addition, is permitted.
11. Post these matters on 23.09.2026 to await the first compliance  
re: completion of the co-option exercise and constitution of the  
State Bar Councils.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Having perused the interim order dated 19 th March, 2026 passed by the
Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad1 under challenge, we
propose to dispose of the special leave petition without even issuing notice to
the respondents.
3. While hearing a challenge to a First Information Report 2 in a writ petition 3
1 High Court
2 registered on the complaint of the petitioner
3 Criminal Miscellaneous Writ Petition No.25763/2025

## Page 227

under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the High Court has practically
granted relief of bail in anticipation of arrest to the accused; not only that, , the
High Court has restrained the investigating officer from filing the charge-sheet
(though investigation has been allowed to continue). In so ordering, the High
Court appears to have considered the co-ordinate Bench decision of this Court
in  Pradnya Pranjal Kulkarni Vs. State of Maharashtra & Anr. 4. Indeed,
reference to such decision might not have been too much of a relevance insofar
as the merits of the case at hand is concerned since it is on a procedural aspect.
The  decision  that  could  be  relevant  in  the  fact  situation  is  Neeharika
Infrastructure Private Limited Vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors. 5
(particularly, paragraph 13) of a three-Judge Bench of this Court; however, it
does not appear that the High Court had the benefit of considering the same.
4. Be that as it may, we find that the writ petition was made returnable upon
service of notice on 14th May, 2026. 
5. Learned counsel appearing for the complainant/petitioner submits that the
matter was neither heard on 14 th May, 2026 nor is any next date of hearing
shown on the website of the High Court. 
6. In the interest of justice, we feel that the interim order passed by the High
Court ought to be limited so that prior to its expiry, the parties are heard and a
final decision is taken by the High Court expeditiously. We, therefore, limit the
interim order till 15 th October, 2026, for the present, subject to such further
order that the High Court may pass on hearing the parties.
7. We request the High Court to decide the challenge laid in the writ petition
bearing in mind the decision in  Neeharika Infrastructure Private Limited
4  (2026) 6 SCC 813 = 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1948
5  (2021) 19 SCC 401 = 2021 SCC OnLine SC 315

(supra) by fixing a date of hearing in the week commencing 21 st September,
2026. 
8. Should the High Court be disabled, for any reason whatsoever, to decide
the writ petition finally before 15 th October, 2026, the impugned interim order
may  not  be  extended  without  granting  opportunity  of  hearing  to  the
complainant/petitioner. 
9. The special leave petition is, accordingly, disposed of on the aforesaid
terms. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of. 
10.  All points and contentions on merits are left open for the parties to urge
before the High Court for a decision by it.

                             O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners. 
2. The present petition is directed against the order
dated 15.11.2023 passed by the High Court of Orissa at
Cuttack in Writ Appeal No.510 of 2023, by which, the
appeal filed by the petitioners against the order of the
1

## Page 239

DIARY NO.24541/2024
learned Single Judge dated 20.06.2022 passed in W.P.C.
(OAC) No.2485 of 2018 has been dismissed on the ground of
delay.
3. Today, learned counsel for the petitioners has drawn
the attention of this Court to the orders passed by this
Court  in  matters  where  Writ  Appeals  filed  by  the
petitioners were dismissed by the Division Bench of the
High Court on the ground of delay, but was remitted for
fresh consideration while awarding cost to the respective
writ petitioners. 
4. We have considered the matter. Indulgence given by
this Court at a particular point of time and in the facts
and circumstances of the particular case(s) cannot be
construed as a licence to the petitioners to continue with
the default and keep filing petitions/applications with
huge delay. After the judgment passed by this Court in
Civil Appeal No.2803/2025, titled “ State  of  Odisha  and
Others  vs.  Sudhansu  Sekhar  Jena ”  and  other  connected
matters dated  21.02.2025 , still the present petition has
been filed on 07.05.2024 with an initial delay of 100 days
and thereafter, followed up by another delay of 534 days
in refiling. This is a stark indicator to the fact that
the petitioners have been very casual and callous with
regard to maintaining the time limit fixed for filing of
such petitions/applications.
2

## Page 240

DIARY NO.24541/2024
5. Having regard to the aforesaid, the Court finds that
the High Court has committed no error in refusing to
condone the delay. We also find that the present delay
also further disentitles the petitioners from any relief
by this Court.
6. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  stands
dismissed on the ground of delay alone.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The petitioner has assailed the impugned judgment and order
19.03.2024 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Patna in
Criminal Appeal(DB)Petition No.1263 of 2018 affirming the order of
the 1st Additional District and Sessions Jyudge, Katihar in Sessions
Trial No. 172 of 2015/CIS No.308 of 2016, by which he was convicted

## Page 242

2
for the offence punishable under Section 302/34 of the Indian Penal
Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life and to
pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-(Rupees Ten Thousand). 
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner sought to persuade this
Court to interfere with the impugned judgment, primarily on the
ground of parity. It was submitted that the allegations against the
petitioner and the co-accused were similar in nature, and the co-
accused have either been acquitted or have been extended the
benefit of reduction of sentence to the period already undergone.
It was further submitted that the petitioner has already undergone
almost twelve years of incarceration and that the injured wife of
the deceased who is said to be the principal eyewitness at the time
of the murder/assault on the husband, is not an eyewitness to such
murder.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner, however, submitted that,
having regard to the period of incarceration already undergone by
the petitioner, at least his case may be directed to be considered
for premature release in accordance with the policy applicable in
the State, upon his fulfilling the requisite eligibility criteria.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the State submits that the case
of the petitioner would be considered by the Competent Authority in
accordance with the applicable policy.
6. Having regard to the aforesaid, without interfering with the
conviction and sentence of the petitioner, we direct the Competent
Authority to consider the case of the petitioner for premature
release, in accordance with the applicable policy, as and when the

## Page 243

3
petitioner completes the requisite period of incarceration and
other eligibility criteria as stipulated.
7. It is also made clear that, in terms of the directions given
by a Coordinate Bench of this Court dated 18.02.2025 in Suo Motu
Writ Petition (Crl.) No.4 of 2021, the State is required to
consider cases of premature release in a time-bound manner.
8. With the aforesaid observations and directions, the Special
Leave Petition stands disposed of. The respondent-State of Bihar is
directed to complete the process of consideration of the case of
the petitioner under the policy of the State Government for
premature release in terms of the aforesaid order.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

on 20.01.2012. It appears that despite having received the
notice and knowledge about the stay order of the Tribunal, the
respondent no. 10 filed a writ application, bearing CWJC No.
10787 of 2012, before this Court concealing the aforesaid
facts, for implementation of the order of the Tribunal, dated
15.07.2011, passed in Case No. 149 of 2010”
4. Contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the finding of
the Single Judge to the effect that notice was received by him on 28 th January,
2012, is incorrect. To buttress his argument, he has invited our attention to
paragraph 9 of the appeal petition filed before the Division Bench where a
specific statement is made to the following effect:
“9. …..The appellant humbly submitted that after accepting
the his joining and after lapse of about two months i.e.
29.8.2012, the order dated 16.12.2011 passed by this Hon’ble
Court  in  CWJC  No.22411/2011  (Ann-6  of  present  writ
application) was communicated to the appellant through the
speed post. Since the order of the appellate Tribunal has
already been complied so there is no question of dis-
obedience. ...”
5. We need to verify which version is correct.
6. Issue notice, returnable in six weeks.
7. The entire scanned records of CWJC No.17244/2015 together with CWJC
No.10787/2012 and LPA No.888/2024 shall be placed before this Court by the
Registrar General of the High Court within four weeks of receipt of this order.
8. It is made abundantly clear that if the version of the petitioner is
ultimately found to be incorrect and this Court discerns an attempt on his part
to mislead the Court, he may be saddled with exemplary costs apart from denial
of a hearing on the merits of the challenge.
  (RASHMI DHYANI PANT)                       (SUDHIR KUMAR SHARMA)
